Synopsis:
This goblin is guarding the entrance to a town his squad have occupied. The residents are long-dead, the town abandoned, and so he's taken it upon himself to rechristen the village as 'Bogrot'.

Cluster Contexts:
- FOR_GoblinAmbush_CheckpointGuards.json: The player has come upon an abandoned village the goblins have seized and renamed “Bogrot”; the original residents are dead and the goblins now hold the entrance. One or more bored, aggressive goblin guards (Booyahg is the snarky leader archetype) are on duty and will taunt, demand goods, and usually threaten violence rather than negotiate. Off-screen goblins may be moving into ambush positions on rooftops or already surrounding the party depending on prior stealth/perception checks, and the player may be on the ground or up with the goblins. A strange glowing symbol appears on the goblins and elicits a supernatural reaction in the player during the exchange. Unless the party includes a drow or successfully talks the goblins down (via persuasion/intimidation checks), the default outcome is that the goblins will attack.
- GOB_Checkpoint_Guard001.json: All guards at the checkpoint point the player to the guard with this dialog. He is an evil, nasty character who has no reason to go easy on the player. Should ooze disdain. This is the first goblin we meet and their weasly, cruel, wicked nature should stand out.
The goblin will let a non-allied player in only if they smear worg shit on their face. Yuck.
- GOB_Checkpoint_Guard004.json: Goblin grunt guarding a checkpoint. Laconic; gruff.
- LOW_KurwinCoffin_KoboldLooter.json: Automatically initiated dialogue after players bash/prise open a coffin with Bugthimble, a tetchy and mistrustful Kobold, just trying to live her best life looting the coffin and the nasty adventurers dug her upt! She wears a face covering helmet.Players have either dug here expecting to find "Enough valuables to settle matters between us" as the note they found said (Tough letter, found on the Courier by Scratch) or just decided to dig up a grave for fun.
- NGB_FOR_Village_Trespassing.json: You’ve walked into a small village now occupied by goblins and run straight into a bored checkpoint guard (usually voiced as a she) posted under the snarky leader Booyahg. Other goblins may be posted on rooftops or closing in depending on earlier sneak/perception checks, and the guard is inclined to taunt, threaten, or attack trespassers for fun unless the player can defuse the situation. A strange glowing symbol briefly appears on the goblins during the encounter and can provoke a supernatural reaction in the player. Hidden checks (sneak/perception/intimidation/persuasion) and the player’s apparent race (non-drow defaults to violence) will determine whether the exchange becomes a fight or the guard grudgingly lets you pass.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Goblin Warrior: 'Allo and welcome to Bogrot! Now, kindly - giz all your stuff. || [context] NodeContext: A goblin's closest approximation of courtesty, faintly mocking. He's loudly welcoming you to the town he has dubbed 'Bogrot' (node 23)
- Narrator: *A strange symbol glows, marked on their flesh, and something within you stirs in response.* (node 46)
- Player: 'Bogrot'? (node 16)
- Goblin Warrior: Local soil-scratchers probably called it something else, but they's dead a hundred years. (node 57)
- Goblin Warrior: So now it's Bogrot. And you got to give over your goods. (node 28)

Sample 2:
- Goblin Warrior: Go on - more of us inside. (node 18)

context: You’ve come upon an abandoned village the goblins have seized and proudly renamed “Bogrot”; the original residents are long-dead and the checkpoint is now held by bored, aggressive goblin guards. The single guard you meet is snarky and nasty (the Booyahg‑type leader archetype), scoffing at you, demanding your goods, and more likely to threaten or attack than negotiate. Other goblins may be posted on rooftops or slipping into ambush off‑screen, and one of the goblins bears a strange glowing symbol that elicits a brief supernatural reaction in the player. Unless you’re a drow or manage a successful persuasion/intimidation check (or meet the goblin’s gross entry condition, e.g., smearing worg excrement), the default outcome is hostility.
